key_reasoning.reason: Five areas touched: the ConfigLoader service (src/utils/config.ts records which keys .env added; src/env/types.ts), a new shared model-origin module (src/utils/model-origin.ts: origin tracking plus describeModel display text), the agent launch core (AgentCLI exports CODEMIE_MODEL_ENV_ORIGIN / CODEMIE_PROFILE_MODEL; BaseAgentAdapter renders the banner for every agent), the copilot-cli plugin and its bin/codemie-copilot.js launcher (saved --model pick), and the profile status CLI command (profile/index.ts, display.ts). Base L for 4+ components across layers with a new shared abstraction, bumped to XL because it touches core shared utilities.

Diffstat reports 17 files changed (1051 insertions, 256 deletions), which is the 16+ XXL band. About 5 are new (model-origin.ts and its test, copilot-cli.saved-model.ts and its test, model-override-parity.test.ts) and about 12 are modified, across src/utils, src/env, src/agents/core, src/agents/plugins/copilot-cli, src/cli/commands/profile, bin and .ai-run/guides. 7 of the 17 are test files and 1 is a guide, so the XXL score overstates the amount of production code.

Second-highest group (M, tied with technical_risk and affected_layers). The goal (show the effective model and what it overrides) is clear, but the diff shows design decisions settled during the work: three origins (shell / dotenv / saved), treating a .env value as dotenv only while process.env still holds it, matching Windows env keys case-insensitively, and marking an override only when the model differs from the profile model.

Agrees with the nearest project example, l/profile-provider-decoupling (total 23, L), which has the same shape: an XL component scope across config, CLI and agent areas, and an XXL file count. This change scores lower on risk and layers because it has no persistence or data migration.

red_flags_applied: Component Scope bumped from L to XL: touches core shared utilities (ConfigLoader in src/utils/config.ts, and BaseAgentAdapter's launch banner shared by all agents). The 'affects multiple workflows or agents' flag lands on the same BaseAgentAdapter change, so it was not counted twice.
